title: C2PA provenance across four hops — admission pass (signed ≠ delivered ≠ instrument ≠ published)
prepared_for: Admission pass — Piotr Reder (eucomplyhub) as independent admission authority (2026-10-02)

propositions.statement: the case-3 manifest DECLARES the claim generator 'OpenAI Media Service API' and a signing certificate (subject CN 'OpenAI Media Service', issuer 'OpenAI OpCo, LLC'), signed 2026-09-28T15:40:40Z
propositions.basis: case3 c2patool: claim_generator_info.name 'OpenAI Media Service API'; signature_info.common_name 'OpenAI Media Service'; signature_info.issuer 'OpenAI OpCo, LLC'. NB issuer = the signing certificate's issuer, not necessarily the signing entity — the two are not asserted to be the same

propositions.statement: the case-3 manifest DECLARES the image as AI-generated (digitalSourceType trainedAlgorithmicMedia; c2pa.created by ChatGPT/gpt-image)
propositions.basis: case3 c2patool: actions.v2 c2pa.created, digitalSourceType=…/trainedAlgorithmicMedia

propositions.statement: the case-1 SIGNED manifest declares Black Forest Labs / FLUX.2 as the generating model (claim generator 'Black Forest Labs API'; softwareAgent + modelName 'FLUX.2')
propositions.basis: case1 c2patool: claim_generator_info 'Black Forest Labs API'; modelName 'FLUX.2'; issuer 'Black Forest Labs Inc.'

propositions.statement: the case-2 SIGNED manifest declares fal.ai as claim generator and softwareAgent, with NO model named (issuer 'fal - Features & Labels Inc.')
propositions.basis: case2 c2patool: claim_generator_info 'fal.ai'; softwareAgent 'fal.ai'; assertion label 'ai.fal.info'; no modelName field

propositions.statement: the pack README labels case-2 'fal, Z-Image' (results table and folder name case2_higgsfield_fal_zimage) — Piotr's record of the model he selected in Higgsfield, not a statement from the signed manifest
propositions.basis: README results table + folder name 'case2_higgsfield_fal_zimage' — a SELECTION-RECORD channel (what Piotr selected in Higgsfield), distinct from the signed manifest (which names only fal.ai). ADMITTED by Piotr (editorial change; subject, channel, grade and scope unchanged)

propositions.statement: the case-2 SIGNED manifest establishes the generating model as 'Z-Image'
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH — 'Z-Image' is NOT in the signed manifest (which names only fal.ai, no model); the model identity rests on the README / Higgsfield selection record, a channel distinct from the signed declaration. Reason class: evidence/relationship (asserted on a different channel from the one that is signed)

propositions.statement: the signed manifest ESTABLISHES that OpenAI actually produced this image (declaration → truth)
propositions.basis: a manifest is a DECLARATION, graded as a declaration; the signing credential is untrusted under the run config (no trust list) and no independent production-record channel is admitted — declared ≠ established

propositions.statement: the delivered PNG (cases 1–2) passes the C2PA data-hash integrity check (a valid C2PA artefact UNDER that check)
propositions.basis: CONTRADICTED by the C2PA data-hash check on the delivered bytes (assertion.dataHash.mismatch → Invalid) — an instrument-independent hash comparison. Scoped to that check, not an absolute 'valid file' property (Hop 3 holds the version/trust half of 'Valid' separately)

propositions.statement: the delivered PNG differs from the validating representation by one identified tEXt('hf-job-id') chunk — removing that chunk restores the c2pa DATA-HASH MATCH
propositions.basis: chunk_order.txt: delivered = IHDR tEXt(hf-job-id) caBX IDAT… IEND vs removed = IHDR caBX IDAT… IEND; after removal the c2pa.hash.data matches (instrument-independent). The full 'Valid' verdict ALSO depends on the certificate/trust half (config-dependent — Hop 3); cases 1–2 are Valid on both core 0.90 and 0.91 (nothing further isolated). 'Content' here = bytes covered by the data hash (a tEXt chunk), not the rendered pixels; this does not establish who produced or signed the underlying image

propositions.statement: Higgsfield is the actor that injected the hf-job-id chunk into the delivered file
propositions.basis: Piotr's INFERENCE from the chunk's name and value; README 'Not claimed' — Higgsfield has not confirmed it. Reason class: evidence/relationship (a confirmation could resolve it)

propositions.statement: the provenance of the delivered thumbnail (webp) can be established from the delivered bytes
propositions.basis: c2patool on 3_thumbnail_as_delivered.webp: 'No claim found' — a distinct representation with no provenance channel. Reason class: evidence/relationship (no channel on this artefact)

propositions.statement: c2patool 0.27.22 with no trust list returned Valid for case 3 (signingCredential.untrusted only)
propositions.basis: case3 c2patool.txt: validation_state 'Valid'; only failure code signingCredential.untrusted

propositions.statement: the case-3 export is valid as an INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENT property of the file
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH — reason class: INSTRUMENT / under-characterisation. The verdict is a function of validator version and trust configuration, not of the bytes alone (see H3-verdict-version-dependent). Pinning the validator version + config does NOT establish intrinsic validity — it establishes a DIFFERENT, instrument-relative proposition ('valid under validator X, config Y'); instrument-independent validity stays CANNOT ESTABLISH

propositions.statement: the case-3 validity verdict DEPENDS on validator version + trust config (c2pa-core 0.90.0 Valid; 0.91.0 Invalid 'certificate missing required EKU'; Valid again with an OpenAI EKU OID allow-listed)
propositions.basis: DISCOVERY stays attributed to Hlias Staurou. ADMITTED here via Piotr's OWN macOS reproduction (c2pa-python 0.37 & 0.38, core 0.90 & 0.91), case 3 v2 — his v1 run matched Hlias's log line-for-line. Which certificate in the chain 0.91 rejects on (leaf / intermediate / TSA) was NOT isolated; no judgment on whether the 0.91 change is correct. Cases 1–2: Valid on both versions

propositions.statement: the LinkedIn-served image bytes — the six size variants inspected 2026-09-29 — carry an in-file C2PA manifest
propositions.basis: CONTRADICTED by Piotr's in-page inspection of six served size variants (2026-09-29, 20–1280px): progressive JPEG, JFIF only, no APP11/JUMBF segment, no OpenAI reference. (Piotr did NOT record a 'c2pa' string search; the zero jumb/'c2pa' byte-scan on the 480×599 variant is Hlias's and stays his, not admitted here.) No APP11/JUMBF segment ⇒ no in-file C2PA manifest. ADMITTED by Piotr after a substantive change — final characterization confirmed by Piotr; FactNotebook incorporated the revised wording (admission is Piotr's, not FN's)

propositions.statement: the LinkedIn-served 480×599 JPEG is the same image as the case-3 export, downscaled (content match)
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH in this admitted reconstruction — the only support was Hlias Staurou's PSNR measurement (served 480×599 vs v2 export = 32 dB vs ~8 dB controls), which Piotr did not run and did not admit on Hlias's behalf. It remains a DECLARED EXTERNAL RESULT attributed to Hlias; with no admitted observation, the content-match is not established here. (It was ESTABLISHED in the FN-admitted version FN-ce30f1089141d0fa; the authority's decision changes the state — this is No Exempt Node, demonstrated not declared.)

propositions.statement: the served JPEG was produced from those exact signed bytes
propositions.basis: the PSNR establishes content-match + manifest-absence, NOT byte-provenance: 'same image downscaled' ≠ 'came from those exact bytes'. Reason class: evidence/relationship

propositions.statement: on a SEPARATE ChatGPT image (posted 2026-10-01, not the case-3 post), the LinkedIn 'cr' badge DISPLAYS manifest data (OpenAI Media Service API; OpenAI OpCo, LLC; issued 2026-10-01)
propositions.basis: Piotr opened the 'cr' badge 2026-10-01 on a different image — directly observed display (same Polish LinkedIn UI, same labels, issued 2026-10-01). ONLY the display is established here: that image's served bytes were NOT inspected, so whether they lack the manifest is NOT established for this image. The displayed ≠ in-file conclusion rests on case 3 (H4-badge-displays-case3). ADMITTED by Piotr

propositions.statement: on the case-3 post itself, the LinkedIn 'cr' badge DISPLAYS provenance values matching the case-3 manifest (app OpenAI Media Service API; publisher OpenAI OpCo, LLC; issued 2026-09-28)
propositions.basis: Piotr opened the case-3 post badge on 2026-10-01 (the served-bytes inspection was 2026-09-29): app OpenAI Media Service API, publisher OpenAI OpCo, LLC, issued 2026-09-28 — matching the case-3 manifest FIELDS (badge app = claim_generator 'OpenAI Media Service API'; badge publisher = signature_info.issuer 'OpenAI OpCo, LLC'; issued = signed date 2026-09-28). Viewed in the Polish LinkedIn UI: 'Używana aplikacja lub urządzenie: OpenAI Media Service API', 'Publikujący: OpenAI OpCo, LLC', 'Wydano 28 września 2026' (English rendering faithful). On the SAME image LinkedIn DISPLAYS the manifest's data while the served file carries no manifest — displayed ≠ in-file, on case 3 itself. ADMITTED by Piotr

propositions.statement: the case-3 'cr' badge reads the displayed values from a C2PA manifest embedded in the served JPEG
propositions.basis: CONTRADICTED within the scope of the inspected files: the served bytes carry no manifest (H4-served-carries-manifest), so there is no embedded manifest in the served JPEG for the badge to read from

propositions.statement: the source the case-3 badge reads these displayed values from is established
propositions.basis: that the badge SHOWS these values is observed (H4-badge-displays-case3); reading from an embedded manifest in the served JPEG is excluded (H4-badge-reads-embedded CONTRADICTED); the ACTUAL source it uses (a LinkedIn-side store, the original upload, …) remains unobserved. Reason class: evidence/relationship
